name: Linezolid
executiveSummary: Oxazolidinone. Adult **600 mg PO/IV every 12 h**. Pediatrics < 12 years **10 mg/kg every 8 h**; ≥ 12 years **10 mg/kg every 12 h** (max 600 mg/dose). Active against MRSA and VRE.
indications:
## Indications

- Pneumonia, skin/soft-tissue infections, and bacteremias due to resistant gram-positives (MRSA, VRE) when other options are unsuitable.

## Precautions

- Myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia) with courses > 10–14 days — check CBC.
- Neuropathy / optic neuritis with prolonged use. Weak MAOI — serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs/MAOIs.
- Limit excess tyramine. Hypoglycemia with antidiabetics.

> PO 100% bioavailable — early oral step-down.

adulto.presentation: Tablets 600 mg; IV bag 600 mg/300 mL (2 mg/mL).
adulto.dose: **600 mg PO or IV every 12 h**. Typical duration 10–14 days (longer only under ID with monitoring).
adulto.administration: Ready IV: 30–120 min; avoid Y-site mixing when possible. PO with or without food.
adulto.notes: IV irritant (phlebitis). Yellow bag color does not mean loss of potency.

pediatrico.presentation: Tablets 600 mg; IV 2 mg/mL; compounded suspension by center.
pediatrico.dose: Preterm < 7 days: **10 mg/kg every 12 h**. Neonate to 11 years: **10 mg/kg every 8 h**. Ages 12–18: **10 mg/kg every 12 h** (max **600 mg/dose**, **1200 mg/day**).
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight up to the adult ceiling.

neonatal.dose: **10 mg/kg/dose every 8–12 h** by postnatal/gestational age (early preterms every 12 h).
neonatal.notes: Follow NNU card; monitor platelets on prolonged courses.

stability:
## Stability

- IV bag: per manufacturer; protect from excessive light if required.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, diarrhea, headache, candidiasis. Thrombocytopenia/anemia, neuropathy, serotonin syndrome, lactic acidosis (rare, prolonged use).
